name: GJ 33
description: A nearby orange dwarf, 70% of the Sun's width: its disc was measured by interferometry.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 33: radius in solar radii, 0.6954 +/- 0.0041, from this work (CHARA)

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 33: mass 0.753 solar masses from the K-band mass-luminosity relation of Henry & McCarthy (1993), not a dynamical mass

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 33: effective temperature in K, 4950 +/- 14, from this work (CHARA)

text.card: A nearby orange dwarf whose disc was measured by interferometry: 70% of the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Interferometry gives it 0.6954 solar radii; with its total light, that makes its surface 4,950 K.
